comment: integration test - spins up a real, separate child kdb-x process, loads real modules via QPATH,
and calls depcheck.init[] for real, proving two things test.csv structurally cannot: that a real
signalled failure actually terminates a real host process (non-zero exit, real error on stderr),
and that a genuine zero-failure success path completes cleanly end to end - unreachable in test.csv
since di.timer, always loaded there as a live negative control, permanently fails its own contract
the child must be kdb-x-capable (needs use/QPATH), unlike a plain q peer, so this deliberately reuses
the currently-running process's own binary via /proc/<pid>/exe rather than guessing from QHOME -
QHOME on this dev machine resolves to a pre-kdb-x q build with no use keyword at all
note k4unit runs every before row first then the asserts - so results are captured in befores and checked in trues
resolve the currently-running process's own binary - guaranteed kdb-x-capable, no QHOME guess, no hardcoded path
confirm the resolved binary actually exists on disk
skip this entire suite cleanly if the binary could not be resolved
scratch directory derived from QPATH at runtime - no hardcoded path
create the scratch directory
